        "body": "## Summary

`tsd_dec_ctx_get` caps `ctx->digits` so that `(Int)D2U(rhs->exponent-lhs->exponent)`
in `decUnitCompare` cannot overflow, but it reserves one too few:

```c
// make sure (Int)D2U(rhs->exponent-lhs->exponent) does not overflow
ctx->digits = MIN(DEC_MAX_DIGITS,
    INT32_MAX - (DECDPUN - 1) - (ctx->emax - ctx->emin - 1));
```

`D2U(d)` expands to `((d)+DECDPUN-1)/DECDPUN`, which C evaluates as
`((d+DECDPUN)-1)/DECDPUN`. The intermediate `d+DECDPUN` is what has to stay
inside `int`, not the final value, so the cap needs `DECDPUN` of headroom
rather than `DECDPUN-1`.

With the current cap the widest exponent gap is `INT32_MAX-DECDPUN+1 = 2147483645`,
and comparing the two ends of the range overflows:

```console
$ jq -n '1e999999999 > 1e-1147483646'
vendor/decNumber/decNumber.c:6257:28: runtime error: signed integer overflow:
2147483645 + 3 cannot be represented in type 'int'
true
```

It is reachable from input data alone, not just program text:

```console
$ echo '[1e999999999,1e-1147483646]' | jq -c 'sort'
```

`sort`, `min`, `max`, `unique`, `group_by` and `sort_by` all hit it.

`tests/jq.test:696` has triggered this on every run since it was added for #2825,
but CI has no sanitizer build, so nothing reports it.

## Fix

Reserve `DECDPUN` instead of `DECDPUN-1`. The widest gap becomes
`INT32_MAX-DECDPUN`, so the intermediate lands exactly on `INT32_MAX`.

## Trade-off

This costs one decimal digit of dynamic range: the smallest representable
exponent moves from `-1147483646` to `-1147483645`. I diffed a build with and
without the change over 3781 programs covering literals and comparisons across
the whole exponent range; 17 differ, all of them within one decimal place of the
minimum exponent, e.g. `1e-1147483646` now prints `0E-1147483645` instead of
`1E-1147483646`. Everything else is byte-identical.

That seemed the right side to err on, since it is the same precision-for-range
trade already made in #2825, and the cap exists for exactly this purpose. The
alternative is to make the arithmetic inside `D2U` unsigned, which would keep
the current range but means patching vendored decNumber at a macro used
throughout the library. Happy to switch if you prefer that.

## Test plan

- Added two cases to `tests/jq.test`: the comparison at the new widest gap, and
  the clamped minimum exponent. The second fails before the change
  (`Expected 0E-1147483645, but got 1E-1147483646`) and passes after.
- `make check` with `-fsanitize=address,undefined`: 30/30 pass, no runtime
  errors. Before the change the same build reports 1 failure and the overflow
  above.
- The first case is not discriminating without a sanitizer, since the overflow
  happens to land on the correct branch; it is there to pin the new boundary.

c9a5156, the commit that closed it, and the reproducer in its own commit message
still triggers it there, so it looks like that part of the claim did not hold:

```
c9a5156 (Dec 2023):  runtime error: signed integer overflow: 2147483645 + 3
b904884 (master):    runtime error: signed integer overflow: 2147483645 + 3
```

The real fix in that commit enlarged the result buffer for `decNumberCompare`,
which is unrelated to `D2U(exp)`.

`tsd_dec_ctx_get` caps `ctx->digits` so that `(Int)D2U(rhs->exponent-lhs->exponent)`
in `decUnitCompare` cannot overflow, but it reserves one too few:

```c
// make sure (Int)D2U(rhs->exponent-lhs->exponent) does not overflow
ctx->digits = MIN(DEC_MAX_DIGITS,
    INT32_MAX - (DECDPUN - 1) - (ctx->emax - ctx->emin - 1));
```

`D2U(d)` expands to `((d)+DECDPUN-1)/DECDPUN`, which C evaluates as
`((d+DECDPUN)-1)/DECDPUN`. The intermediate `d+DECDPUN` is what has to stay
inside `int`, not the final value, so the cap needs `DECDPUN` of headroom
rather than `DECDPUN-1`.

With the current cap the widest exponent gap is `INT32_MAX-DECDPUN+1 = 2147483645`,
and comparing the two ends of the range overflows:

```console
$ jq -n '1e999999999 > 1e-1147483646'
vendor/decNumber/decNumber.c:6257:28: runtime error: signed integer overflow:
2147483645 + 3 cannot be represented in type 'int'
true
```

It is reachable from input data alone, not just program text:

```console
$ echo '[1e999999999,1e-1147483646]' | jq -c 'sort'
```

`sort`, `min`, `max`, `unique`, `group_by` and `sort_by` all hit it.

`tests/jq.test:696` has triggered this on every run since it was added for #2825,
but CI has no sanitizer build, so nothing reports it.

Reserve `DECDPUN` instead of `DECDPUN-1`. The widest gap becomes
`INT32_MAX-DECDPUN`, so the intermediate lands exactly on `INT32_MAX`.

This costs one decimal digit of dynamic range: the smallest representable
exponent moves from `-1147483646` to `-1147483645`. I diffed a build with and
without the change over 3781 programs covering literals and comparisons across
the whole exponent range; 17 differ, all of them within one decimal place of the
minimum exponent, e.g. `1e-1147483646` now prints `0E-1147483645` instead of
`1E-1147483646`. Everything else is byte-identical.

That seemed the right side to err on, since it is the same precision-for-range
trade already made in #2825, and the cap exists for exactly this purpose. The
alternative is to make the arithmetic inside `D2U` unsigned, which would keep
the current range but means patching vendored decNumber at a macro used
throughout the library. Happy to switch if you prefer that.

- Added two cases to `tests/jq.test`: the comparison at the new widest gap, and
  the clamped minimum exponent. The second fails before the change
  (`Expected 0E-1147483645, but got 1E-1147483646`) and passes after.
- `make check` with `-fsanitize=address,undefined`: 30/30 pass, no runtime
  errors. Before the change the same build reports 1 failure and the overflow
  above.

  happens to land on the correct branch; it is there to pin the new boundary.

c9a5156, the commit that closed it, and the reproducer in its own commit message
still triggers it there, so it looks like that part of the claim did not hold:

```
b904884 (master):    runtime error: signed integer overflow: 2147483645 + 3
```

which is unrelated to `D2U(exp)`.

part.text:
Fixed. The root cause: decNumber's `decCompare` computes `rhs->exponent - lhs->exponent` in an `int32_t`, which overflows when comparing numbers parsed with extreme exponents (up to ±1999999998 after string parsing), leading to the out-of-bounds access in `decUnitCompare` and the segfault.

The fix (matching upstream jq commit `3fa10e8` for issue #2825) is in `tsd_dec_ctx_get` (src/jv_dtoa_tsd.c:97): cap `ctx->digits` at `INT32_MAX - (emax - emin - 1)` so the maximum adjusted exponent (`emax`) minus the minimum adjusted exponent (`emin - digits + 1`) never exceeds `INT32_MAX`. Any literal outside this range is clamped by `decFinalize` during parsing, making the exponent subtraction in `decCompare` safe.

Verified:
- `./jq -n '3E506760210 < 63E-6855002263'` and `[ 3E506760210, 63E-6855002263 ] | sort` no longer crash
- `./jq -n '66e-5338725652!=1E816161611'` (the related OSS-Fuzz 61235 reproducer) works
- Full `make check` passes, including `tests/jqtest` with the `#2825` boundary cases (`1e-1147483648`)
